title: Capability bundles and version discovery API for model pinning and runtime constraints
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a unified 'capability bundle' and discovery API that surfaces per-model and per-version constraints and features to clients and routing logic. This ticket covers: (1) a stable JSON schema for capability bundles (limits, context_window, supported_features, quality_profiles, resource_hints, affinity_hints), (2) a discovery endpoint that lists model versions and their capability bundle references for pinning and runtime routing, and (3) backwards-compatible adapters for existing model-manifest endpoints. Goal: enable deterministic version pinning, automated fallback selection, and runtime kernel/quantization hints for better cost/latency routing.
acceptance_criteria: A /discovery/models endpoint returns an array of versions with capability_bundle refs and ETags
Capability bundle schema is versioned (schema_version) and documented in Confluence
Client SDKs (Python/Node) deserialize bundles and expose context_window, limits, supported_features as first-class fields
Routing layer uses resource_hints and affinity_hints to select compatible model variants in Dedicated/Dynamic pools
Telemetry emits a capability_bundle_id with each inference request for quality/regression correlation
Unit tests for schema parsing and integration tests for discovery endpoint caching and ETag behavior
Migration plan published and old manifest endpoints continue functioning for at least one release cycle
technical_notes: Schema fields should be primitive or arrays only (no nested objects beyond one level) to simplify SDK maps and Dynamo storage
Use top-level schema_version (semver-like) to allow incremental extension of capability facets
limits block: {max_tokens_per_call, max_context_tokens, max_batch_size} and units must be explicit
Affinity hints: hardware_affinity_tags and fallback_variant_keys to support graceful degradation
Decision: return capability bundles as immutable resources referenced by stable IDs to enable caching and telemetry correlation
Trade-off: embedding detailed perf curves vs. simple percentile summaries. We will publish p50/p95 latency_ms and token_cost_estimate to balance payload size and usefulness
Cache strategy: discovery responses TTL=300s, capability bundle TTL=24h; use ETag for client-side caching
Security: capability bundles may include sensitive size hints, run security review before public release (see security_review_required)
Backward compatibility: Adapter layer will translate legacy manifest fields to new bundle schema with deprecation warnings in logs

2025-01-20 - Luis Garcia: Implemented prototype discovery handler that returns capability_bundle refs. Pushed branch feature/discovery-proto. Need review from runtime team on resource_hints semantics. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1289

2025-01-24 - Mei Chen (runtime): Reviewed resource_hints and requested inclusion of preferred_kernel and memory estimate. Raised concern about exposing exact memory footprints — suggested ranges instead. Action: change memory_bytes_estimate to memory_range_bytes.

2025-01-28 - Product (Jon Rivera): Added requirement to include quality_profiles with a short description and canonical id for monitoring regressions. Suggested adding p50/p95 latency and token_cost_estimate to bundle.

2025-02-01 - Security (Priya Rao): Flagged that some resource hints may be considered implementation details. Requested security review and ACL on discovery endpoint for Private customers. Marked security_review_required=true.

2025-02-04 - Luis Garcia: Addressed Mei's feedback, switched to memory_range_bytes and added fallback_variant_keys. Updated tests for ETag behavior. Integration tests failing intermittently for cache invalidation — investigating race condition in cache invalidator.
2025-02-05 - Asha Patel: Sync with SDK owners scheduled (2025-02-06) to ensure deserialization ergonomics. Roadmap updated to include docs and migration notes.
migration_plan: Phase 1: Publish capability bundle schema v1 and discovery endpoint as opt-in internal API (runtime-1.20-alpha)
Phase 2: SDKs consume bundles and routing uses resource hints for Dedicated pools (runtime-1.20-beta)
Phase 3: Deprecate legacy manifest fields in public docs, keep adapter layer for backward compatibility (runtime-1.21)
Phase 4: Monitor telemetry for two release cycles before full public rollout
